interest: This file provides concise contemporary insight into early Japanese government initiatives to counter the Great Depression through state-sponsored industrial reorganization. Established in 1930 under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the Temporary Industrial Rationalization Bureau (Kōgyō Gōrika Kyoku) sought to stabilize distressed industries; this record highlights the initial moves toward cartelization, production control, and corporate amalgamation in the woolen textile sector. For economic historians of the interwar period, it illustrates how U.S. diplomats monitored Japan's structural economic adjustments and industrial concentration policies.
overview: This file contains State Department records from August 1930 classified under decimal number 894.62222 (pertaining to animal husbandry, stock raising, and wool in Japan). It consists of a Document File cross-reference sheet and an accompanying extract from Despatch No. 219 (originally filed under 894.00 P.R./32) transmitted from the American Embassy in Japan under Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville. The documents report on the July 1930 inaugural meeting of the woolen industry committee of the Temporary Industrial Rationalization Bureau, which deliberated the rationalization of production and marketing along with the fundamental rationalization of the Japanese wool trade through corporate amalgamation.

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet indexing an excerpt from Despatch No. 219 concerning rationalization in the Japanese wool industry.
subfiles.summary: This document file note cross-references report No. 219 filed under 894.00 P.R./32, dated August 1, 1930, from the U.S. diplomatic mission in Japan under Chargé Edwin L. Neville (mistranscribed as Seville). It records that the first meeting of the woolen industry committee of the Temporary Industrial Rationalization Bureau took place in July 1930 to discuss rationalizing production and sales. The note further highlights that fundamental rationalization via industrial amalgamation of the wool sector was considered and that a copy of the report extract is attached.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Despatch No. 219 on Wool Industry Rationalization

subfiles.about: An extract from Despatch No. 219 detailing the first meeting of the woolen industry committee of the Temporary Industrial Rationalization Bureau.
subfiles.summary: This document is the attached extract from Despatch No. 219 reporting on the first meeting of the woolen industry committee under the Temporary Industrial Rationalization Bureau (misrendered in the text as Nationalization Bureau). The committee considered methods for rationalizing production and sales across the sector. It also deliberated on fundamental rationalization through the amalgamation of firms within the Japanese woolen industry.
subfiles.title: Extract on First Meeting of the Woolen Industry Committee
